title: It’s Not the ATS — Your Resume Isn’t Clear Enough (Fix This)
description:
If you’ve been blaming the ATS for why your resume isn’t getting interviews… you’re not alone. But it’s likely not the ATS.

Most job seekers think they need to “beat the system” with the right keywords, formatting, or tricks. But that’s not what recruiters are actually looking for.

In this video, I break down:

How recruiters actually read resumes (hint: it’s FAST)
Why unclear resumes get skipped—even when you’re qualified
The real reason your resume isn’t converting to interviews
How to fix your bullet points so your value is obvious immediately

Because recruiters aren’t looking for the most keyword-optimized resume…
They’re choosing the one they understand the fastest.

If your resume isn’t getting interviews, it’s not because you’re not qualified.
It’s because your value isn’t clear fast enough. If you need more support creating a resume that gets picked, check out my Get Seen Guide below:

transcript: You're not getting rejected because of the ATS. It's because your value isn't clear fast enough. I know this is where there's a lot of confusion right now. Companies are using technology and AI, and your resume might go through some level of screening. But a human is still deciding who gets interviewed, and they're not studying your resume, they are scanning it. They're trying to quickly answer one question. Do I understand this person and can they do this job? They're making that decision in seconds. If they have to slow down, reread, or try and figure you out, they simply move on. So, if you've been obsessing over keywords and trying to beat the system, you're focusing on the wrong thing. So, let's fix that. I'm Kate Krschner, career strategist, job search nerd, your career bestie, and I have spent the last 20 years helping job seekers get hired. So, let's get into it. Here's what happens when you write your resume for a system instead of a person. You end up with content that sounds polished, but says absolutely nothing. It looks a little something like this. Responsible for managing teams and driving strategic initiatives to improve operational efficiencies. That sounds impressive, but it's very vague. Now, compare that to this. Streamlined cross-functional workflows, reducing project turnaround time by 25% and improving team efficiencies. Now, the recruiter doesn't have to figure it out, the value is obvious. Here's another example. Instead of writing work done improving internal processes, you write identified process inefficiencies and implemented workflow improvements that reduced manual work by 10 hours per week. That's the difference. One sounds like a responsibility, the other proves impact. And this is exactly where most resumes fall apart. Because recruiters are not looking for job keywords, they are looking for proof. What did you do, how did you do it, and what happened because of it? And this is the shift that changes everything. Instead of trying to beat the ATS, you need to focus on clarity and positioning. Your resume should make three things immediately clear. What you do, what you're great at, and the results you've delivered. That's where your bullet points matter. Instead of saying team player, prove it. Something like collaborated with cross-functional teams across operation and sales to streamline workflows, reducing turnaround time by 25%. Or partnered with a team of six to identify process gaps and implemented solutions that increased output by 30%. That's what makes a recruiter believe you. Now, this doesn't mean you ignore keywords completely. Yes, your resume should align with the job description. Yes, you should reflect the language of the role, but not at the expense of clarity. Because a resume full of keywords that no human can quickly understand does not get interviews. Clarity always wins. So, let's bring this home. You don't need to beat the ATS, you need to be clear. Because recruiters are not picking the most keyword optimized resumes, they're picking the one they understand the fastest. If your resume isn't getting interviews, it's not because you're not qualified, it's because your value isn't clear fast enough. And that's exactly what I help people fix every single day. You can check out my get seen guide, I'll link it below, and if you want real, no-BS career advice that actually moves the needle, stick with me, I've got you. Make sure to like and subscribe for more videos with insider information.
